trigger_ar: وَفِى ثَمُودَ إِذْ قِيلَ لَهُمْ تَمَتَّعُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ
after: A temporary reprieve is announced to the named people
reason: ثَمُودَ explicitly repeats the focus's second community, while تَمَتَّعُوا۟ حَتَّىٰ حِينٍۢ marks a limited interval before the surrounding account of their fate. This is a real historical echo, though the cited verse itself does not yet show the destruction or its visible trace.

trigger_ar: فَعَتَوْا۟ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ فَأَخَذَتْهُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ
after: The people rebel while looking on as punishment overtakes them
reason: فَعَتَوْا۟ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِمْ states rebellion, and وَهُمْ يَنظُرُونَ makes their sight present when judgment comes. These actual words sharpen the focus's paradox of a people with perception who still failed to take the right course.

after: The gaze is described as neither swerving nor overreaching
reason: ٱلْبَصَرُ directly activates the perception image in مُسْتَبْصِرِينَ, but 53:17 describes a rightly steady gaze rather than misguided people. The contrast offers a limited foil to the focus's failed use of insight.

after: The first ʿAd are explicitly said to have been destroyed
reason: أَهْلَكَ عَادًا ٱلْأُولَىٰ states the destruction of the focus's named people outright. This supplies a direct historical fate behind the surviving evidence of their dwellings.

trigger_ar: كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌۭ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ

reason: عَادٌۭ and كَذَّبَتْ repeat the focus's community and identify its rejection, while عَذَابِى وَنُذُرِ joins punishment to warning. This directly activates the focus's historical caution about what followed their course.

trigger_ar: تَنزِعُ ٱلنَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍۢ مُّنقَعِرٍۢ
before: the remains of a destroyed community

reason: تَنزِعُ ٱلنَّاسَ and أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ present a vivid bodily aftermath in the ʿAd account. It parallels visible ruin but describes people rather than the focus's dwellings.

after: The named people are explicitly said to deny their warners
reason: ثَمُودُ is the focus's second named people, and كَذَّبَتْ بِٱلنُّذُرِ states their rejection of warnings. This directly fits the focus's historical pattern of clear warning met by a people who went astray.

trigger_ar: إِنَّآ أَرْسَلْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ صَيْحَةًۭ وَٰحِدَةًۭ فَكَانُوا۟ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلْمُحْتَظِرِ

reason: صَيْحَةً وَٰحِدَةً and كَهَشِيمِ ٱلْمُحْتَظِرِ give a compact image of Thamud's destruction in its surrounding narrative. The verse evokes aftermath, but does not mention dwellings or later observers.

trigger_ar: وَلَقَدْ أَهْلَكْنَآ أَشْيَاعَكُمْ فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍۢ
after: Destruction is paired with an invitation to remember
reason: أَهْلَكْنَا أَشْيَاعَكُمْ and فَهَلْ مِن مُّدَّكِرٍۢ connect past destruction to present reflection, echoing the focus's warning purpose. The ayah supplies no specific dwelling or named people, so the link remains broad.

after: Persistent adherence to grave sin is described
reason: يُصِرُّونَ عَلَى ٱلْحِنثِ ٱلْعَظِيمِ depicts sustained wrongdoing, which weakly echoes the focus's harmful practice-field. It has no beautification, Satan, or path language.

trigger_ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلنَّجْوَىٰ مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ لِيَحْزُنَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
after: Secret counsel is attributed to Satan and made distressing
reason: مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ names the agent, while لِيَحْزُنَ describes a harmful effect on believers. This weakly expands the focus's account of satanic action but does not show the same adornment or route-blocking image.

trigger_ar: ٱسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ فَأَنسَىٰهُمْ ذِكْرَ ٱللَّهِ

reason: ٱسْتَحْوَذَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنُ directly portrays Satan gaining control, and فَأَنسَىٰهُمْ ذِكْرَ ٱللَّهِ names the resulting inward diversion. These words activate the focus's account of his influence on a community.

trigger_ar: يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم بِأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَيْدِى ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ فَٱعْتَبِرُوا۟ يَٰٓأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَبْصَٰرِ
before: dwellings as witnesses to failed security

reason: دِيَٰرِهِمْ, حُصُونُهُمْ, and يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُم make habitation and failed protection explicit, while فَٱعْتَبِرُوا۟ يَٰٓأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَبْصَٰرِ turns the scene into a lesson for observers. The sequence strongly activates both the focus's ruined dwellings and its contrast between evidence and insight.

trigger_ar: كَمَثَلِ ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ إِذْ قَالَ لِلْإِنسَٰنِ ٱكْفُرْ

reason: ٱلشَّيْطَٰنِ and ٱكْفُرْ show an adversary prompting a destructive choice, with the following words depicting his abandonment of the person. This is a related warning about influence, but not the focus's beautified deeds or blocked path.

trigger_ar: مَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِٱلْمُهْتَدِينَ

trigger_ar: فَتَرَى ٱلْقَوْمَ فِيهَا صَرْعَىٰ كَأَنَّهُمْ أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍۢ

after: The fallen are likened to hollow palm trunks
reason: صَرْعَىٰ and أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ خَاوِيَةٍ make the bodies of ʿAd visible after the wind, a tangible counterpart to the focus's historical trace. The image is of fallen people, not their dwelling places themselves.

before: turning away from a right reminder

before: people with insight who rejected guidance

after: The focus's named community appears in a compact paired precedent

after: Iram is identified through its pillars
reason: إِرَمَ ذَاتِ ٱلْعِمَادِ activates the traditional Iram/ʿAd association and supplies the image of monumental construction. That image enriches the focus's mention of ʿAd's surviving dwellings as traces of a once-established people.

before: the former places of a powerful people
after: The unmatched scale of Iram's construction is stressed
reason: مِثْلُهَا فِى ٱلْبِلَٰدِ praises the unmatched scale of the place identified just before as Iram, giving a weak built-environment echo to the focus's dwellings. This verse itself does not state that the settlement is ruined or that its remains testify.

after: A scourge of punishment falls on them
reason: فَصَبَّ عَلَيْهِمْ رَبُّكَ سَوْطَ عَذَابٍ recalls judgment on the peoples named earlier in the passage. It supplies the punishment behind the focus's visible aftermath but does not mention their dwellings.

after: The worst of the people rises into action
reason: أَشْقَىٰهَا continues the Thamud narrative and points to the person who undertakes the decisive act. Because this verse lacks the name, the deed, and the ruins, its link to the focus is only contextual and slight.

after: A whisperer who withdraws is named as a source of harm
reason: ٱلْوَسْوَاسِ ٱلْخَنَّاسِ evokes hidden prompting associated with Satan, weakly calling up the focus's deceptive agent. These words do not say that deeds are beautified or a road is blocked.

reason: ٱلْجِنَّةِ وَٱلنَّاسِ completes the description of whisperers as coming from unseen and human sources. This broadens the focus's adversarial image only weakly, since the cited verse does not name Satan or depict the focus's specific action.

before: the way from which people were turned

The shared clarity and sign vocabulary makes the surrounding ruins a deliberate evidence motif, while يَعْقِلُونَ recalls the perception the focus says the earlier people possessed.

after: The next parable presents a house too weak to protect its occupants
reason: The focus's مَّسَٰكِنِهِمْ sits near the spider's بَيْتًا and ٱلْبُيُوتِ in the following ayah. This shifts the dwelling image from visible remains to fragile shelter, suggesting that residence or apparent protection cannot secure those who rely on the wrong support.
